q: How many subsets does a set of n distinct elements have?
why: Each element is independently in or out: 2 · 2 · … · 2 = 2ⁿ.

q: How many permutations of 4 distinct elements are there?
What is `res` after this runs with nums = [1, 2]?
code:
res, path = [], []
def bt(start):
    res.append(path)
    for i in range(start, len(nums)):
        path.append(nums[i])
        bt(i + 1)
        path.pop()
bt(0)
why: Every append stores the SAME list object, which is empty after all the pops. Append `path[:]` instead.

q: Combination Sum lets you reuse a candidate. What changes in the recursion?
options: Recurse with i instead of i + 1
why: Staying at i allows the same candidate again; never going below i avoids duplicate orderings.

q: Subsets II (input has duplicates, sorted): which skip rule avoids duplicate subsets?
options: if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
Use a set of tuples only
why: At one depth, only the first of equal values starts a branch. `i > 0` would also block [1, 1] where the second 1 is picked deeper.

q: Generate Parentheses: when may you add ')'?
why: A closing bracket must close something already opened.
